excluded_families.rationale: Their data domains do not contribute to visual-composition measurement and importing them would create irrelevant coupling.
Clinical functionality and data are outside PelicanBench's benchmark, ontology, and publication scope.
A generic protocol or estate standard is preferred over coupling to every fork or packaging repository.

These are valuable first-party data and application assets, but their domains and interfaces do not contribute to V1 visual-composition measurement. They remain discoverable through the owner namespace rather than becoming PelicanBench dependencies.

policy.benchmark_firewall: Training datasets, hidden tasks, scorer feedback, and human calibration data remain separate unless a prespecified study permits transfer.
policy.coupling: Prefer versioned files, CLIs, Agent Skills, schemas, and HTTP protocols over copied implementations or source-level imports.
policy.evidence: Implemented, contracted, and pattern-adopted records require repository evidence; external operational availability is reported separately.
policy.exclusion: Domain-adjacent repositories are not dependencies merely because they share an owner or technology stack.
policy.hf_inventory: The 2026-08-01 owner profile was reviewed at the model, dataset-family, and Space-family level. Directly relevant model and training-provenance assets are explicit; unrelated domain datasets and Spaces are dispositioned by family.
policy.selection: Integrate first-party assets only when they supply a distinct benchmark capability, a reusable estate standard, or a publication/runtime boundary.
